note: How content moves, renders, and gets looked at: the address grammar a reference shares across the repo, the delivery modes pages/toss-render.html accepts, the toss routes that map a content type to the page that renders it, and the `showing` block, which answers the question those three do not: given a thing you changed and a person who will open the link, which mechanism reaches it. Read by show-repo's Map view (Showing tab), which is the live version of this file and the reason CLAUDE.md no longer restates any of it. The `routes` block is the owner of toss-render.html's TOSS_ROUTES literal, which stays inlined so the critical render path takes no fetch; tools/test/routes-manifest.test.mjs holds the two in step.
precedence: Every parameter below is read fragment first, query as fallback: toss-render for its own params, and the renderer pages through lib/kits/url-params.js. Put a payload in the fragment, which never reaches a server and so escapes the roughly 8KB cap the Pages edge enforces with a 414 (PR #165). An address is short, so either form works, and a routed toss delivers ?src= through toss-render's params shim rather than over the wire.

grammar.role: One way to name a file in any repo, at any ref. The ':' before the path is unambiguous because git forbids ':' in ref names; no @ref means the repo's default branch.

usedBy.where: a repo's pages catalog and stage.files

modes.note: The page rides in the fragment, so nothing is hosted and nothing reaches a server. Absolute-URL CDN dependencies work; same-repo relative ones do not.
The uncompressed sibling of #gz=. Same sandbox, longer URL.
Points the frame at a URL rather than carrying the bytes. A site sending X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors will refuse to load.

Fetched live through the contents API, so private repos and un-deployed branches render. Same-origin means the frame could read this origin's stored token, which is why the allowlist refuses any other owner outright. The browser-local token means a fresh or in-app browser may 404; fall back to #gz= or a published artifact.

A typed toss: the key names a renderer from the routes below, the value addresses the content. Resolves onto address mode, so the caller addresses the CONTENT and toss-render stays a schema-blind router that never parses the envelope.

The renderer side of the split, not a toss-render param. A routed toss resolves into this: toss-render renders the renderer page and the params shim delivers ?src= to the page's own read. Reaching a renderer directly with ?src= works the same; the route is shorthand, not a gate. Renderer pages read it fragment first like everything else, so #src= is accepted too.

routes.renders: A chat or trawl results envelope: search hits across conversations, annotated and rendered together.

Data as something readable rather than a raw blob: a CSV, a JSON array, a log, in a multi-mode viewer (table, tree, preview, code, raw). Bare bytes need no wrapper; an items envelope adds several files with a default view each.

A document to adjudicate a shortening against, word-diffed into accept-by-default edits. Bare text fills the left column and leaves the shorter version to you or the in-browser model; an envelope carrying both sides opens straight into review.

showing.note: Getting a subject in front of a viewer. Three independent variables decide the mechanism, and conflating them is what made this hard to state: WHAT the subject is, WHICH version of it, and WHO is opening the link. `preview` is not a topic, it is one value of `version`.

mechanisms.label: Canonical URL
mechanisms.subject: a deployed page
mechanisms.reaches: the page as everyone else sees it
mechanisms.use: The thing is already live. Always prefer it.

mechanisms.label: ?use= lib pin
mechanisms.subject: a deployed page, its LIB only
mechanisms.reaches: anything lib/ or dist/ does, including what it does to the tab itself
mechanisms.misses: the page's own inline shell: its markup, and any x-data defined in the file
mechanisms.use: The change lives in lib/ or dist/ and the page file itself is unchanged.
mechanisms.trap: Pages serves the page FILE from the default branch, so a shell change shows the old shell wrapped around new lib, silently and with nothing reporting the mismatch.

mechanisms.label: Toss, address mode
mechanisms.subject: any file
mechanisms.reaches: the branch's real page file, shell and all
mechanisms.misses: anything the shell does to the TOP-LEVEL document: title, favicon, history, navigation
mechanisms.use: The change is in a page's own shell. Put ?use= in the QUERY so the renderer around it matches too.

mechanisms.label: Nested toss
mechanisms.subject: toss-render itself
mechanisms.reaches: the renderer's own internals: routing, frame mounting, rendering, address parsing
mechanisms.misses: the top-level document, same as above; a nested shell is never the tab
mechanisms.use: The change IS toss-render. Address the branch's renderer, hand it the page as a trailing fragment.

mechanisms.label: Toss, carried payload
mechanisms.subject: a page
mechanisms.reaches: any reader, no token, nothing hosted
mechanisms.misses: same-repo relative dependencies; only absolute-URL CDN deps resolve
mechanisms.use: The reader has no token, or you want the bytes pinned into the link itself.

mechanisms.label: Claude artifact
mechanisms.subject: a self-contained page
mechanisms.reaches: a reader in the Claude app, where the GitHub token may be absent
mechanisms.misses: anything needing the network: artifact CSP blocks every external request
mechanisms.use: The link will be opened in the Claude app AND the page can be baked self-contained.

mechanisms.label: No link reaches it
mechanisms.subject: a page shell acting on the top-level document
mechanisms.misses: everything: ?use= keeps the old shell, and a toss is never the top-level document
mechanisms.use: Send an inspected headless screenshot and say plainly that no link can show it. The escape is not a better link but moving the code into lib, where ?use= reaches it.

picker.note: The mechanism is derivable rather than remembered: it follows from which files a branch changed. show-repo knows a branch's changed files already.
